To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean willingness to pay of all respondents to avoid the proposed offshore wind farm was about $0, but that there were large differences in willingness to pay between individuals with different characteristics.
the wind farm was a good that most people would be willing forego under compensation but that the mean willingness to pay varied considerably across individuals.
the wind farm was on average a good that people were willing to forego for compensation and that willingness to pay to forego the wind farm varied considerably across respondents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the challenge of how to deal with data from a nonmarket valuation study with large degree of ambiguity and heterogeneity in the valuation context.
the challenge of valuing an environmental bad in a context where there is no consensus on whether it constitutes a good or a bad.
a nonmarket valuation problem where the good in question is a bad or a good, depending on the valuation method used.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wind farm was a bad for some and a good for others, but on average it was a good.
the proposed wind farm would have a net positive impact on welfare for those who would be near, and a net negative impact on welfare for the rest.
the wind farm was a bad that people were willing to pay to have, but only for a subset of the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wind farm is a bad for those living near the proposed wind farm who perceive the turbines as “ugly” and a good for those living far away and who perceive the turbines to be “pretty”.
the wind farm was a bad for some and a good for others.
, in this context, the wind farm was a good for those who perceived it to be a good, and a bad for those who perceived the wind farm as a bad.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important not to a priori label a non-market good as either a bad or a good.
it is important to take into account all preference information when estimating welfare measures, even when the preferences are ambiguous.
it is important to account for heterogeneity in preferences when estimating welfare measures.
